summary.title: The minimum home kit
points: You need progressable weights, a mat and bands.
A starter set of a 12 kg bell, dumbbells to 10 kg and a mat covers the upper body.
Legs and hips soon need more load.
Skip machines, barbells, treadmills and gadgets.
About 2 × 2 m of floor; protect it under kettlebells.

exercises.scenario: A friend wants to start at home on a small budget.

questions.prompt: What's essential?
options: A treadmill, because cardio is the base for fat loss
Weights you can progress with, plus a mat

questions.prompt: What can replace a bench at first?
options: The floor and a sturdy step
Nothing; a bench is required for presses

exercises.scenario: Your kettlebell has left marks on a wooden floor.

questions.prompt: What's the simple fix?
options: A mat or rubber tiles under the training spot
Switching to machines, which never touch the floor

questions.prompt: How much space do you need?
options: A dedicated room of at least 20 square metres
About 2 × 2 m, with room to press overhead

summary.title: Dumbbells
points: Fixed: quick and robust, but a range takes space and money.
Spin-lock: cheap, slow to change; check the collars.
Selector: fast and compact, bulky, fragile if dropped.
Lower-body moves often need about 20–30 kg per hand within a year (practice estimate).
Small steps (1–2.5 kg) matter, especially for presses.

exercises.scenario: You have little space and want a full range of weights.

questions.prompt: Which type fits?
options: Fixed rubber hex dumbbells in every weight up to 30 kg

questions.prompt: What's the main care point with spin-lock dumbbells?
options: Keep them in a dry box
Never drop them, since the dial mechanism breaks

exercises.scenario: Your press stalls going from 10 kg to 12.5 kg dumbbells.

questions.prompt: Why?
options: Dumbbells over 10 kg aren't suitable for pressing
A 25% jump is large for a small muscle group

questions.prompt: What would help?
options: Skipping the press entirely and only doing push-ups

summary.title: Kettlebells
points: Cast iron: cheaper; the bell grows with weight. Competition: same size at every weight, pricier.
Common sizes in 4 kg steps: 8, 12, 16, 20, 24 kg…
Swings and deadlifts take the heaviest bell; presses and get-ups the lightest.
Common starting advice: 16–24 kg for men, 8–16 kg for women, depending on history.
A 12 kg bell is a good press bell; 16 or 20 kg is the likely next one.

exercises.scenario: You own a 12 kg bell and swings feel easy.

questions.prompt: Which bell do you add?
options: 8 kg, so that you can swing faster and longer

questions.prompt: What stays the job of the 12 kg?
options: Swings and deadlifts, which need the lightest bell

exercises.scenario: A shop offers a competition bell at twice the cast-iron price.

questions.prompt: Do you need it for home training?
options: Yes: cast-iron bells give a weaker training effect
Yes: competition bells are required for swings

questions.prompt: What do you check on any kettlebell?
options: That it's painted in the brand's competition colours
A smooth handle with no sharp seams and a flat base

summary.title: Mat, bands, bar and bench
points: Bands add load that grows with stretch, and give pulling without a bar.
A set of three strengths covers most needs.
Door-frame bars need a solid frame, can mark trim, and have weight limits.
A bench helps later; a 6–10 mm mat is comfortable for floor work.
Buy bands early: cheap and useful.

exercises.scenario: Your doors have narrow, decorative frames.

questions.prompt: How do you add vertical pulling?
options: A screw-in bar fitted to the decorative frame anyway
A band anchored high for pulldowns

questions.prompt: What else covers the back well?
options: Overhead presses with a heavier bell

exercises.scenario: You're choosing between a bench and a band set.

questions.prompt: Which first, and why?
options: Bands: cheap, and they fill the pulling gap
The bench, because presses are impossible without one
questions.explanation: The floor covers presses at first.

questions.prompt: How does a band's resistance behave?
options: It stays constant throughout the movement
It rises as the band stretches
It depends on the room temperature only
questions.explanation: That's what makes them different from weights.

summary.title: Finding your starting weights
points: A test set finds the right weight for a rep target.
Reps in reserve (RIR): how many more reps you could have done.
More than ~4 left: go heavier. 1–3 left: your weight. Target missed: lighter.
First two weeks: err on the light side while learning technique.
20+ goblet squats at 12 kg means 12 kg is too light for 10–15-rep sets.

exercises.scenario: Target 10–15 reps. You finish 15 rows with about 6 left.

questions.prompt: What do you do?
options: Keep the weight and add a set, since it's still useful

questions.prompt: You manage 9 reps of a press and can't do a 10th. What then?
options: Keep the weight; 9 is close enough

exercises.scenario: Your baseline: 26 goblet squats at 12 kg.

questions.prompt: What does it tell you?
options: 12 kg is too light for 10–15-rep squat sets
12 kg is perfect for strength work in the 3–5 rep range
questions.explanation: You need more load for legs.

questions.prompt: When should you go lighter than the test suggests?
options: In the first two weeks, while learning technique
Never; always use the heaviest weight possible

summary.title: What to buy, and when
points: Buy for the bottleneck: what limits training most right now.
Usual order: heavier lower-body load, then bands, then a bar if the door allows, then bench and tiles.
Second-hand cast iron is usually fine; check for cracks and rough handles.
Prefer adjustable dumbbells if space or money is tight.
Re-check every 4–8 weeks; the kit planner applies these rules.

exercises.scenario: Baseline: 28 goblet squats at 12 kg, 18 push-ups, no bar, no bands.

questions.prompt: What goes in 'now'?
options: A 16 kg kettlebell and a band set
A bench and heavier dumbbells for pressing
questions.explanation: Legs are the bottleneck; bands are cheap.

questions.prompt: When do you re-check?
options: Only once, at the start, then never again

exercises.scenario: A second-hand 20 kg kettlebell is for sale.

questions.prompt: What do you check?
options: The original receipt and the warranty card
questions.explanation: Cast iron is durable if sound.

questions.prompt: Which principle decides the order of purchases?
options: Buy the most expensive item first
Buy what looks best in the room first
questions.explanation: What limits you most right now.

summary.title: Weights and extras
points: Essentials: progressable weights, a mat, bands.
Dumbbells: fixed, spin-lock or selector; small steps matter.
Kettlebells: cast iron is fine; heavier bells for hips, lighter for presses.
Bands fill the vertical-pull gap; a door-frame bar if the frame allows.
A bench and tiles can wait.

exercises.scenario: Small flat, standard budget, kit: 12 kg bell and dumbbells to 10 kg.

questions.prompt: Which dumbbell type suits the space?
options: A full rack of fixed hex dumbbells from 2 to 30 kg

questions.prompt: Which kettlebell job stays with the 12 kg?
options: Swings, which need the lightest bell

questions.prompt: Explain why bands are an early buy.
questions.modelAnswer: They're cheap and portable, they add load that grows with stretch, and anchored high they give a pulldown, filling the vertical-pull gap when you have no pull-up bar.

exercises.scenario: A friend plans to buy a bench, a treadmill and a competition kettlebell first.

questions.prompt: What would you suggest instead?
options: A heavier cast-iron bell or adjustable dumbbells, and bands
The same, since that's the standard home-gym order

questions.prompt: Why skip the treadmill?
options: Treadmills build more muscle than weights
Sport and walking already cover cardio
questions.explanation: It doesn't fill a strength gap.

summary.title: Choosing loads and buying
points: Test sets with reps in reserve find working weights.
More than ~4 left: heavier; 1–3: keep; target missed: lighter.
Baseline results show where the kit runs out.
Buy for the bottleneck, usually lower-body load first.
Re-check every 4–8 weeks with the kit planner.

exercises.scenario: Week one of your new programme.

questions.prompt: What do you do for each exercise?
options: Use the heaviest weight you own for every exercise
Run test sets and log the working weights

questions.prompt: Your goblet-squat test leaves 6 reps in reserve at 12 kg. What follows?
options: The lower body needs heavier load
The upper body needs heavier load

questions.prompt: Describe how to run a test set in three steps.
questions.modelAnswer: Pick a rep target, for example 10–15. Do one set with a guessed weight and good form. Estimate reps in reserve: more than about 4 left, go heavier; 1–3, keep it; target missed, go lighter.

exercises.scenario: After 6 weeks, presses stall and squats are easy with the new 16 kg bell.

questions.prompt: What's the next bottleneck?
options: A bench, because presses need back support

questions.prompt: What tool helps decide?
options: The kit planner, with your re-test results

summary.title: Equipment: the whole picture
points: Minimum kit: progressable weights, a mat and bands.
Dumbbells: selector or spin-lock for small steps and little space.
Kettlebells: cast iron; heavier for swings and squats, lighter for presses.
Bands fill the pulling gap; a bar only if the door allows.
Test sets with reps in reserve set your loads.
Buy for the bottleneck and re-check every 4–8 weeks.

exercises.scenario: You plan your purchases from a baseline of 24 goblet squats at 12 kg.

questions.prompt: What's the first buy?
options: A lighter 8 kg bell to master swing technique
questions.explanation: 20–29 reps at 12 kg points to 16 kg.

questions.prompt: What's the cheap early buy that fills a gap?
How do you set the working weight on day one?
options: The weight printed on the programme
The heaviest weight you can lift once
Test sets with reps in reserve

exercises.scenario: Three months on, you've bought a 16 kg bell and bands.

questions.prompt: When do you consider the next purchase?
options: Immediately, to keep the motivation going
When re-tests show a new bottleneck

questions.prompt: Which item is optional for most home trainees?
Explain 'buy for the bottleneck' with your own example.
questions.modelAnswer: Buy what limits training most right now. For example: if 12 kg goblet squats are too easy, a 16 kg kettlebell comes before a bench, because legs are what can't progress.
